angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 243,495 km at 47.78 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 20.9279 +/- 0.0133 mas (same row, RUWE 1.19): 47.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.35 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-206 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract): 243,495 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.35 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-206 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3383 +/- 157 K from Giacalone et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-206 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163...99G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
